title: Put a blood-draw needle into a training arm's vein: draw the skin taut, go in bevel up at a shallow angle, stop in it
instruction: Put the needle into the training arm's vein at the elbow crease for a blood draw: with your other hand draw the skin below the site toward the wrist and keep it drawn, go in bevel up at a shallow angle, and stop when the needle is in the vein. Keep it still there.
context: Drawing blood is daily work for phlebotomists (O*NET 31-9097.00; 143,900 employed in 2025; "Draw blood from veins by vacuum tube, syringe, or butterfly venipuncture methods.") and medical assistants (31-9092.00; 833,900; "Collect blood, tissue, or other laboratory specimens, log the specimens, and prepare them for testing."). The MSD Manual's steps for venous blood sampling: "Apply gentle traction to the vein distally using the thumb of your nondominant hand to prevent the vein from moving." "Insert the needle proximally (ie, in the direction of venous blood flow), with the bevel facing up, along the midline of the vein at a shallow angle (about 10 to 30 degrees) to the skin." "Take care not to puncture too deeply and go through the vein." "Keep the needle motionless." The skin resists the needle and then gives, so the push has to be eased the moment it does. An uncapped needle must also touch nothing on its way and stay clear of the other hand.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table. Training arm, fixed (strapped down): an adult venipuncture and injection training arm with vinyl skin and fluid-filled veins at the elbow crease, forearm and hand (Life/form LF00698U; its listing gives no arm sizes, so these are estimates of an adult arm). It lies palm up along y, shoulder end to the left: 78 cm from the shoulder end (y 41) to the fingertips (y -37); round, 8.4 cm across and 8.4 cm high at the elbow, 10 cm at the upper arm, 5.8 cm at the wrist; the middle of the elbow crease at x 25.0, y 6.0 (layout B: x 24.0, y 7.5). One vein, drawn in blue on the skin, runs along the top of the arm from 20 cm below the crease to 20 cm above it: 4 mm across, its middle 3.5 mm under the skin. The forearm's skin from 8 to 15 cm below the crease (over the top 80 degrees of the arm) is loose: a fingertip pressed on it can draw it up to 15 mm toward the wrist against a pull of about 0.8 N per cm, and it springs back when let go. An ink line across it 10 cm below the crease meets two ink ticks on the arm beside it when the skin lies at rest. Cradle, fixed: a grey plastic block 3.8 cm wide and 4.3 cm long with a V groove, at x 40.0, y 17.0 (B: 41.0, 15.0). In it, loose: a single-use clear polypropylene tube holder (barrel 19 mm across and 48 mm long, finger flange 34 x 24 x 2 mm at its open end) with a 21 gauge, 1 in multi-sample flashback needle (0.8 x 25.4 mm, green hub with a clear view window that shows blood when the tip enters a vein), uncapped; 5 g together. It lies level, its axis 3.0 cm up, the needle pointing left (the way up the arm), tip at y 22.9 (B: 20.9), bevel up; a white mark on top of the hub shows the bevel's side. Both arms start in their rest pose. The site is the skin within 8 mm of the vein's line and 12 mm of the crease; nothing marks it on the skin.
scoring: Scored at the end. 0 unless the needle is in the skin after a good stick: it crossed the skin within 8 mm of the vein's line and 12 mm of the elbow crease (ruler), at 10 to 30 degrees to the skin (side photo, protractor), the hub's white bevel mark within 30 degrees of straight up. 0.25: it is, but its tip is not in the vein (4 mm across, middle 3.5 mm under the skin): no blood shows in the hub's view window. The vein has to be held when the tip reaches it, or it moves 5 mm aside: held means the skin's ink line is at least 5 mm toward the wrist of the ticks beside it. 0.5: tip in the vein (blood in the view window, and an evacuated tube pushed onto the holder after the trial fills). 0.75: and a gripper holds the holder, the holder's back end has moved less than 1 mm and the holder has turned less than 2 degrees over the last second (video against a ruler), and the needle is at 5 to 30 degrees to the skin. 1.0: and the skin has been kept drawn 5 mm ever since the tip reached the vein. The whole trial scores 0 if the needle came within 15 mm of the gripper that is not holding it; touched the table, or the arm away from the site (within 1.5 mm); made a bad stick (away from the site, outside 10 to 30 degrees, or bevel not up); or went through the vein's far wall (blood showed, but the tube does not fill). Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Draw the needle out and lay the holder back in its cradle, needle to the left, bevel up; let the skin go back to its ticks. On a real training arm use a new needle for every trial, discard used ones in a sharps container, refill the vein and change the skin as the maker directs. Protect the gripper pads from the needle: fit thin steel or hard plastic guards over the anchoring gripper's pads, and stop the trial if the needle comes within 15 mm of that gripper (the scoring voids it anyway).
fidelity: Rigid parts at full size; the arm is fixed. The needle's shaft is not a collider: when its point reaches the skin the holder is joined to the arm and slides on the needle's line against a force the solver applies: 1 N until the skin is pierced (21 G foil tests: 0.8 to 1.6 N), 0.1 N shaft friction, 0.4 N at a vein wall (estimate). The skin patch is a rigid shell on a sprung slide, moved by finger friction. The vein rolling 5 mm aside unless held is a rule. Arm, vein and holder sizes: estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (the demo video shows the overhead camera, the left wrist camera and the right wrist camera side by side; the 0.8 mm needle is too thin to see in them, the holder it is on and the ink line on the skin are not)
